column3: Borel–Weil–Bott covers characteristic zero; modular intermediate cohomology and GL(V)-module extensions for every weight are the obstacle. Incidence weights alone are not full scope.
The report gives v1=2, v2=1 and high-dimensional constructions, not sharp lower bounds in every dimension. Optimizing one weighted hypersurface family cannot certify the global infimum.

The candidate uses Sylvester sequences and recurrent polynomial weights; a counterexample must compare exact pair volumes with the precisely defined standard-coefficient Kollár pair in the same dimension. No candidate certified.

Local polynomial degrees of freedom must be unisolvent and globally H^m-conforming for every m,d. The report explicitly separates nonconforming stabilized elements and finite neurons; neither answers this scope. Later general constructions need checking.

Definition 5 and the actual question are PDF page 19, not the cited 18. A relative Dirac-index inequality with suboptimal constants does not imply equality rigidity for arbitrary incomplete metrics; no equality mechanism supplied.

Problem 7 prescribes both boundary metric and mean curvature plus completeness and a scalar lower bound. Local static extensions near special data do not give necessary and sufficient conditions for arbitrary data.

The report distinguishes C^r results for r>=2, hyperbolic periodic type and genus-two rigidity. The Roth-type r=1 codimension assertion requires endpoint cohomological estimates and a submanifold theorem, absent here.

Exercise 8 already explains n=2, odd n and powers-of-two compression. Decompose odd-primary characters semisimply; the 2-primary minimality still needs module classification. Repackaging the worked exercise is ineligible.

Determining rational points uniformly over all primes is far beyond the p=13 quadratic-Chabauty instance. Stable and regular models in the report aid computations but do not bound all rational points.

Problem 3 concerns the singular locus inside Jin–Xiong's global Monge–Ampère solution orbifold. Explicit polytope examples and low dimensions do not determine its dimension, topology, regularity and exclusion conditions uniformly.

Need the full radical-subgroup classification in bad characteristic for all exceptional families and field sizes; finite group enumeration only yields instances. The report cites F4 weight progress without supplying that classification.

Chevalley-type derivation normalizers are handled in the report, with graph-isomorphism hardness for general normalizers. The missing non-Chevalley simple factors require uniform structural algorithms, not a single Witt example.

For finite input groups, enumerate abelian normal kernels K of X and isomorphisms X/K to G; conjugation induces the quotient action because K is abelian. This gives literal exhaustive enumeration but is an elementary routine algorithm, not a new result or efficient solution.

Literal a_H,b_H in Z[H] make a_H N_H b_H equal their augmentation product times N_H. Thus the stated coefficient domain matters and cannot silently be replaced by Z[G]. d=0 is also trivial. Optimization requires the intended nonzero relation and support conventions from the cited paper; no credit for repair.

An unbounded equalizer search semidecides positive cases but gives no terminating negative certificate. Immersions or injective/marked special cases cited by the report do not decide arbitrary pairs of homomorphisms.

If cyclic free subgroups count, every infinite-order matrix supplies its own basis {M}; that interpretation is a routine wording shortcut. The source's computational Tits-alternative discussion requires a substantive rank and input-field model before claiming an algorithm.

Theorem B gives very special parahorics up to adjoint conjugacy. Refining to J_b(F)-conjugacy requires tracking splitting of adjoint orbits and each component's class, not repeating the maximal-volume theorem.

The cited page already reports rigorous Price tails for compact support. General asymptotically hyperboloidal data have different tails; data decay and incoming radiation must be fixed. A compact-support formula is both published and only a special case.

Finite SAGBI generation is the semigroup finite-generation obstruction. The report already gives permutation-invariant criteria and a new infinite-SAGBI family. Merely restating finite SAGBI existence is circular; no useful general criterion established.

Generating-functional completion imposes consistency across algebra relations; splitting a cocycle need not permit separate Gaussian and jump functionals. Known SU_q(n) and simple-spectrum universal cases in the report are already results.

Topological generation by connected classical and residually torsion-free nilpotent group-dual pieces would force zero residual. The report establishes that route for U_N^+, not O_N^+; a suitable orthogonal generation theorem remains missing.

The report itself singles out the S3 transposition rack with constant cocycle +1; the -1 example is finite dimensional. A candidate must prove infinite dimension, finite GK dimension and genuinely nonabelian support simultaneously, with successor clearance.

The cited direct Quillen equivalence is for n=2; the report's n>2 statement is explicitly 90%-theorem work in progress. Need a genuine equivalence and generators/localization comparison for every n>2, with later results checked.

The construction requires a wall-crossing description preserving symplectic, not just homological or geometric mapping-class, monodromy of every isolated hypersurface unfolding. A_mu and plane-curve examples do not settle it.

The actual numerical question is PDF page 48. The report already has algebraic/geometric criteria and reduces to KT subset data; enumerating rank defects of selected configurations is not necessary and sufficient numerical characterization for all r,k,n.

Need the plus-one generated resolution, level and multiplicity data used in Question 7, not the adjacent supersolvability conjecture. A nearly-free criterion or an example of an unexpected curve is insufficient; targeted section retained separately.

The alternating Kostant q-partition formula is already given. A positive combinatorial interpretation in all other root types is stronger; evaluating the formula or specializing q=1 is no new resolution.

Report distinguishes asymmetric k=4 from solved symmetric k=4 and hypergraph fixed-k cut. Symmetrizing f loses the four-block objective. Need an exact algorithm or oracle lower bound for arbitrary submodular f; approximation results do not resolve it.

PDF page 24 Theorem 1 states the requested time 2^(0.802n) and space 2^(0.401n) algorithm for arbitrary norms and lattices. AKS sieving plus constructive convex-body positioning is the reported mechanism, so this is not a new problem resolution.

Strassen's completeness theorem is already known; flattening ranks and quantum functionals give only subfamilies. A full classification must cover every additive multiplicative monotone functional, not merely exhibit another member.

The report presents a provably convergent inflation hierarchy and a quantum causal polynomial-optimization formulation. Need to distinguish asymptotic convergence, exact attainment and finite termination. Reimplementing a presented hierarchy earns no credit; arbitrary countable constraints preclude an automatic finite certificate claim.

The report separates connected derived supergroup determination from the Picard group of the semisimplification. Missing invertible-object relations and negligible-morphism quotient prevent using the derived-group formula as the answer.

Question 1 quantifies an arbitrary graph class and target H; report then restricts to robustly sparse classes and proves asymptotic bounds. Exhaustive enumeration on n vertices is a tautological finite maximum given a membership oracle, not a substantive universal formula.

Hypercube coloring already gives Omega(n log n); report's O(n log^4 n) does not answer O(n log n). Short rainbow-cycle expansion results are a close successor lead; current full-scope theorem body needed before any new attempt.

Paley graphs attain (n-1)/2 on suitable orders and a general n/2+O(sqrt(n log n)) bound is cited. Exact maximum for each n needs upper bounds and matching constructions, not asymptotic or small-order enumeration.

Report already lists linear bounds for paths, trees and cycles, polynomial for 2-outdegenerate graphs and exponential transitive-tournament obstruction. A structural characterization must distinguish these families at all sizes.

The report states upper bound 2n-3 and Postle's lower construction 7n/6. Thus answer n is already ruled out in the primary. Exact extremum for every n remains distinct from the solved large-n clique EFL conjecture.

Generalized Krichevsky–Trofimov assignments handle the stated small-block range. Larger blocks enlarge unknown alphabets and redundancy; one must control universal redundancy in that regime, not just improve data compression empirically.

General null and alternative hypotheses require matching converse and achievable exponent at each communication rate. Independence tests and expected-rate multihop multiplexing in the report are special regimes, not full resolution.

A single-letter mismatch capacity formula must cover every channel and additive decoding metric; the report supplies converse bounds, not equality. Even the zero-error subproblem blocks treating a computable bound as the capacity.

The primary explicitly says generalized Gaussians fail at p=2 by Jaye–Livshyts–Paouris–Pivovarov. Optimizing over a guessed parametric family or importing Shannon Gaussian extremizers therefore fails full scope.

The exact question occurs on PDF page 22. For any c>=0, rho=c I satisfies data processing and both differences equal c times conditional mutual information, concave at fixed channel. rho=0 already refutes literal uniqueness. This is an elementary normalization defect, explicitly ineligible for discovery credit.

The same paragraph already cites a partial answer for two intervals and sufficiently many blow-up points. A new example must be compared with Cozzi–Fernández 2204.05837; the reduced Robin functional's critical points, rather than a numerical peak plot, are decisive.

The page describes a construction program using Waldenfels/Wentzell data and singular-integral estimates, with planned monograph results. Arbitrary analytic data cannot generate Feller semigroups without positivity, domain and resolvent conditions; those precise hypotheses and reported solution scope need the following theorem pages.

The preceding page defines K1, Kn comodule algebras and commuting integrals. Similarity to quantum symmetric pairs is only motivation; unification must recover all relations and completions including non-A types, not just matching integral formulas.

Atiyah–Segal finite-dimensional gluing is essential. Primary Corollary rules out semisimple oriented theories; it also mentions unoriented exotic sensitivity, so orientation and target must be tracked. A gauge invariant without functorial gluing does not answer it.

The construction of H-minimizing valuation and finite generation is already a deep theorem. Need an explicit nontrivial first degeneration with nondivisorial minimizer; a toric divisorial computation or existence citation is inadequate.

The source distinguishes Weyl characters of induced modules from irreducible L_lambda in positive characteristic. Applying Weyl's characteristic-zero formula does not solve modular characters for every dominant weight and prime.

P1-P4 and the total-degree Chebyshev kernel are specified on pages 38-39. The SDP gives numerical coefficients, not a closed form or analytic optimality for all multivariate orders. Tensor products generally violate the total-degree optimum.

The source recalls Rosen's real-field problem and develops a P-adic analogue with floor axioms a-d. An arbitrary coding of K into finite strings is a wording shortcut; termination and approximation must follow the intended continued-fraction axioms uniformly in K.
